translationRepairs: When Sun Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his grandfather Tong bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, grand general of agile cavalry, duke over the masses, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Yong Province; his father Ji received bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province.

When Sun Teng rose high, the Wei court posthumously granted his grandfather Tong bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the four provinces of Yong, Hua, Qi, and You, grand general of agile cavalry, duke over the masses, left vice director of the masters of writing, and governor of Yong Province; his father Ji was posthumously granted bearer of the staff of authority, palace attendant, commander-in-chief of military affairs in the five provinces of Ji, Ding, Cang, Ying, and Yin, grand commandant, director of the masters of writing, and governor of Ji Province.

Chinese 贈 applies to both Tong and Ji; idiomatic 'received' for Ji drops the posthumous force that literal correctly keeps as 'was posthumously granted'. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of opener of a government office equal in protocol to three imperators.
Fengzhen was dull and dim; in the Wuping era he died while holding the rank of opener of a government office equal in protocol to the Three Ducal Ministers.
三司 denotes the Three Ducal Ministers (Three Offices), not 'three imperators'. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

三司 denotes the Three Ducal Ministers (Three Offices), not 'Three Imperators'. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Because Gao Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, Gao Huan ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Liaoren in Bohai.
Because Gao Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, Gao Huan ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Tiao in Bohai.
渤海蓚人 means a man of Tiao (蓚/蓨) in Bohai; 'Liaoren' misreads 蓚. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Because Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, the Grand Ancestor ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Liaoren in Bohai.
Because Longzhi later had merit in deliberation and counsel, the Grand Ancestor ordered that he be treated as a younger cousin and still declared him a man of Tiao in Bohai.
渤海蓚人 means a man of Tiao (蓚/蓨) in Bohai; 'Liaoren' misreads 蓚. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Gao Longzhi over wine; the emperor was made to sit and was dismissed from office.
Western Wei Emperor Wen once quarreled with Gao Longzhi over wine; Longzhi was implicated and dismissed from office.
Chinese 坐以黜免 marks Longzhi's dismissal after the wine quarrel, not the emperor's; the idiomatic English wrongly dismisses the emperor. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.

Same referent error as idiomatic: 黜免 applies to Longzhi after the quarrel with Emperor Wen, not to the emperor. Independent source review confirms the proposed correction.
An elder sister had become a nun; he served her as a mother would and, in instructing his sons, always put literary principles first.
His widowed elder sister became a nun; he served her as he would his mother and, when instructing his sons, always put literary learning and moral principle first.
事之如母 means he treated his sister as he would a mother, not that a mother was the agent of the service. Independent source review also restores omitted source meaning and natural English.
